newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to cut election campaigns to 36 days.
newsitem.headline: Canada to cut election campaigns to 36 days.

text.p: The Canadian government introduced legislation in Parliament on Monday to make federal election campaigns, already much shorter than U.S. presidential campaigns, even shorter.
The bill would set 36 days as the minimum period for a campaign, down from the present 47 days. There is no maximum duration for campaigns, and they usually last for the minimum period.
The bill would also create a permanent federal voters' list, eliminating the need for door-to-door registration for each election.
"Study after study show that Canadians would prefer a shorter campaign period," said Dan Rogers, spokesman for Solicitor General Herb Gray, who introduced the bill in the House of Commons.
The bill would also result in cost savings, he said.
Prime Minister Jean Chretien's Liberal Party won the last federal election in October 1993, giving it up to five years in power. Chretien is expected to call elections next year.
